blocks.h2: Why Algonquin Homeowners Get a Sewer Camera Inspection

tiles.body: Roots and sags often show up at this age. Know before you close.
Find out whether it's roots, a sag or a break.
Make sure the line and floor drains are sound first.
Check whether a cracked line is letting groundwater in.

blocks.h2: What We Find in Algonquin Sewer Lines
blocks.intro: More than half of the lines here went in between 1990 and 2009. The camera tends to show the same few things.

items.body: Early root intrusion from maturing trees, easy to manage if it's caught early.
Standing water where the line settled after construction.
Often the pipe is fine and just needs cleaning.
Homes in the older part of town may show clay or cast iron with age-related damage.
In 1990s and 2000s subdivisions, the camera often finds one or two low spots where the line settled. Knowing where they are lets you plan a targeted repair.

blocks.h2: Sewer Camera Questions From Algonquin Homeowners

items.q: Is a sewer inspection worth it for a newer home?
items.preview: Yes, if you're buying or having repeat clogs.
items.answer: Yes. Lines from the 1990s and 2000s are now old enough for roots and sags. If you're buying or dealing with repeat clogs, a camera look is the cheapest way to know.

items.q: Can the camera tell how deep the pipe is?
items.answer: Yes. The camera head carries a transmitter, and our locator shows where it is and how deep.

items.q: What if my cleanout is buried?
items.preview: We'll find it or suggest another access point.
items.answer: We can usually locate it. If not, we may go through a toilet or roof vent, or add a new cleanout.

items.q: How long does an inspection take?
items.preview: About an hour for most homes.
items.answer: About an hour for most homes, from finding the cleanout to walking you through the video.

items.q: What does a sewer camera inspection cost in Algonquin?
items.preview: It depends on access and line length. The price comes first.
items.answer: It depends on access and how long the line is. We quote a flat rate before we start.
